question: Whether to approve the stipulation between Georgia Power and Public Interest Advocacy Staff that extends the 2022 Alternate Rate Plan for three years, through December 31, 2028, in place of the base rate case due July 1, 2025.
phase: Joint petition to extend the Alternate Rate Plan, filed May 19, 2025; hearing June 26, 2025

outcome.summary: The Commission voted July 1, 2025 to adopt the stipulation, extending the ARP through December 31, 2028 with base rates unchanged in 2026-2028 except for a separate 2026 storm-cost proceeding, and requiring a general rate case filing by July 1, 2028. It did not adopt GIPL's proposed motion, said it lacks authority to order recusal, and found Georgia WAND's schedule motion untimely.
outcome.source_title: ORDER GRANTING JOINT PETITION OF GEORGIA POWER COMPANY AND THE PUBLIC INTEREST ADVOCACY STAFF AND APPROVAL OF THE STIPULATION TO EXTEND THE ALTERNATIVE RATE PLAN

positions.asked: Asks the Commission to approve, without modification, its stipulation with PIA Staff keeping base rates unchanged for the next three years except storm-cost recovery, and to deny GIPL's and NRDC/Sierra Club/SACE's requests for an illustrative cost-of-service study and other added requirements.
positions.source_title: Rebuttal Testimony of Aaron P. Abramovitz and Matthew S. Berrigan in Support of the Stipulation to Extend the ARP
positions.where: V. Conclusion, p. 9 (also Sections II-III on the cost-of-service requests)
positions.check: with approval of this Stipulation, customer rates will remain stable and predictable for the next three years

positions.asked: Public Interest Advocacy Staff signed the stipulation with Georgia Power and recommends approval, arguing a litigated rate case risked higher rates; it cites the Company's preliminary projection that customers could pay $2.588 billion more over 3 years.
positions.source_title: Direct Testimony and Exhibits of the panel of Tom Bond and Steven Roetger
positions.check: Yes. The settlement agreement will provide much needed relief to customers.

positions.asked: Asks the Commission to amend the stipulation by motion to state that residential and small business customers will not pay costs caused by new large loads, and to require Georgia Power to report hourly load, generation, RTP price, large-load and illustrative cost-of-service data before 2028.
positions.where: Attachment 1, GIPL's Proposed Motion, p. 1 (brief pp. 1-2, 5)
positions.check: GIPL requests the Commission amend the Stipulation by inserting two new paragraphs as follows:

positions.party: Natural Resources Defense Council, Sierra Club and Southern Alliance for Clean Energy
positions.asked: Witness Wilson says the Commission lacks enough information to judge whether the stipulation is just and reasonable and recommends it direct Georgia Power to file an illustrative cost-of-service study and updated resource procurement practices before its next rate case.
positions.source_title: Direct Testimony of John D. Wilson on behalf of Natural Resources Defense Counsel, Sierra Club and the Southern Alliance for Clean Energy
positions.where: Section II, answer to 'What is your recommendation?' (text has no page numbers)
positions.check: I recommend that the Commission direct Georgia Power to file an illustrative cost-of-service study

positions.asked: States that, for purposes of this docket, Walmart does not oppose Commission approval of the joint petition, describing it as a better means of limiting bill increases than a litigated 2025 rate case.
positions.source_title: Direct Testimony and Exhibit of Steve W. Chriss on behalf of Walmart Inc.
positions.check: For the purposes of this Docket, Walmart does not oppose Commission approval

positions.asked: Does not oppose continuing current rates until 2028, but asks the Commission to proceed with the review of the need for Georgia Power's Community Charging program that it says the 2022 rate case order scheduled for 2025.
positions.source_title: Comments of Americans for Affordable Clean Energy on the Stipulation to Extend the Alternate Rate Plan
positions.where: Opening paragraph and final paragraph before signature (text has no page numbers)
positions.check: the Commission should conduct the scheduled review of the Community Charging program to which all parties agreed in 2022

positions.asked: Joint complaint co-signed by Georgia WAND, GCV Education Fund and Center for a Sustainable Coast: asks Commissioners Shaw, McDonald and Echols to recuse, and asks the Commission to deny the rate-freeze proposal (preferred) or appoint an outside administrative law judge.
positions.source_title: Formal complaint and demand for recusal of Commissioners speaking publicly in support of Georgia Power's 3-year rate freeze
positions.check: Deny the rate-freeze proposal. The PSC should conduct a rate-case

positions.asked: Asks the Commission to amend the May 20, 2025 schedule to set intervenor direct testimony no earlier than July 24, 2025, and adjust rebuttal and hearing dates. Vote Solar joined. WAND also co-signed the June 6 recusal complaint.
positions.source_title: Georgia Wand Education Fund’s Motion to Extend the Commission’s Procedural Schedule in Georgia Power Company’s 2022 Rate Case
positions.check: set the deadline for intervenor direct testimony no earlier than July 24, 2025

notes: GCV Education Fund: its own filing in this phase is only its June 26, 2025 intervention, with no stated ask. But it co-signed (Brionté McCorkle, Executive Director) the June 6, 2025 recusal complaint filed under Georgians for Affordable Energy's name, which asks the Commission to deny the rate freeze or appoint an outside ALJ; the order also names it as a filer of that complaint. I therefore did not list it under parties_without_stated_position and folded it into the joint complaint entry; a reviewer may prefer a separate line for it. The complaint was dated June 5 and predates GCVEF's and Georgia WAND's interventions; no intervention by Georgians for Affordable Energy or Center for a Sustainable Coast appears in the filing list, so their 'Intervenor' role is uncertain. Stance calls: GIPL is coded 'supports with changes' because it asks the Commission to amend the stipulation, though it never states support; NRDC/Sierra Club/SACE is coded 'other request' because Wilson calls the record insufficient but does not ask for rejection; AACE is 'other request' (no opposition, separate Community Charging ask; Georgia Power's rebuttal argues that review waits for the 2028 rate case); Walmart's wording is 'does not oppose'. GAM's joinder is based on the filing's title and service page only, since the stipulation text is blank; Utility Management Services, Inc. also joined but is not a filer in the list. Georgia Power filed no post-hearing brief, so its rebuttal is its last word; the joint petition (doc 222693) and direct testimony (doc 222848) state the same request. GIPL's earlier direct testimony (Barnes) and May 21 request for supporting documentation are superseded by its brief. Sierra Club's amended intervention (doc 222940, adding NRDC and SACE) and the 2025 scheduling order attachments have no text. The June 26, 2025 hearing transcript (doc 223463) has no text file. Staff's June 20 errata only made previously redacted numbers public ($853M of $2.589B offset; $1.736B remaining deficiency). The order says the Commission voted July 1, 2025; the written order is dated July 31, 2025 in the list. Other questions in this docket, not covered here: the 2026 storm damage recovery application and PIA Staff stipulation (short order June 2, 2026; Order Adopting Stipulation Aug 4, 2026); Community Charger plan orders (June 12, 2025; Oct 3, 2025; Dec 18, 2025; July 30, 2026); orders on the 2024 and 2025 annual surveillance reports (Dec 24, 2025; Nov 4, 2026); the Nuclear Uprates (NU-1) tariff order (Oct 9, 2026); recurring large load contract, Grid Investment Program and Charge It EV rider filings; and Georgia Power's Nov 9, 2026 response to a Hubbard motion on deposits and bills.
